title: TAE Technologies Signs Helium-3 Fuel Supply Agreement with Black Moon Energy
detail: TAE Technologies and Black Moon Energy Corporation (BMEC) announced a strategic agreement on August 5, 2026 covering a prospective helium-3 fuel supply option and commercial development collaboration for fusion power. BMEC, a privately funded natural-resource and lunar-development company, plans a robotic lunar delineation mission within five years to de-risk a commercial-scale helium-3 production operation, offering TAE an alternative fuel path to its hydrogen-boron (p-B11) aneutronic approach. TAE CEO Michl Binderbauer said the deal 'can facilitate our path to power by providing an alternative fuel supply option.' TAE's first planned fusion power plant, Da Vinci (50 MWe), targets operations in 2031, with future facilities scaling to 350–500 MWe.

title: ORNL Licenses Cryogenic Pellet Fueling Technologies to Type One Energy
detail: On August 5, 2026, at the Nuclear Opportunities Workshop in Knoxville, Tennessee, the US Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) signed a licensing agreement transferring four ORNL inventions — including a tritium-compatible cryogenic pellet gas gun and a tritium-compatible cryogenic screw extruder — to stellarator developer Type One Energy. The technologies address a persistent gap in fuel-pellet production rates needed for continuous deuterium-tritium plasma operations. The deal expands Type One's existing ORNL collaborations, including high-heat-flux component testing and the Innovation Network for Fusion Energy program, and supports the company's Infinity One stellarator prototype at the Tennessee Valley Authority's Bull Run site (targeting commissioning in 2029) ahead of a planned 350 MWe Infinity Two commercial plant.

title: CFS Attains Two DOE Milestones for ARC Commercial Fusion Plant
detail: Commonwealth Fusion Systems announced on August 5, 2026 that it has attained two additional milestones under the US Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program — this time for its commercial successor to SPARC, the ARC fusion power plant, rather than SPARC itself (the subject of CFS's first three DOE milestones). The two milestones recognize completion of an ARC preconceptual design and a technology roadmap detailing the engineering steps required to build the plant. The achievements build on CFS's five peer-reviewed physics-basis papers on ARC published in the Journal of Plasma Physics on June 4, 2026, and follow the company's $1 billion raise on July 30, 2026 that brought total capital to $4 billion.
